reference_title: Rheumatoid arthritis in adults: management (NG100)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 11 July 2018.
supported_statement: Negative rheumatoid factor or anti-CCP antibodies, or a normal acute-phase response, do not remove urgent referral indications in adults with unexplained persistent synovitis and specified joint-pattern or delay criteria.
scope_limitations: Referral despite negative serology; not a seronegative diagnosis.

reference_title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm: diagnosis and management (NG156)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 19 March 2020 and shows no separate last-updated date.
supported_statement: Encourage unscreened men aged at least 66 to self-refer for AAA screening when they have COPD, arterial disease, family history of AAA, hyperlipidaemia, hypertension, or current or previous smoking.
scope_limitations: Risk factors are used for opportunistic screening in unscreened men aged 66 or over. This is not a quantified risk model or a severity/rupture prediction rule.

reference_title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm: diagnosis and management (NG156)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 19 March 2020 and shows no separate last-updated date.
supported_statement: Consider aortic ultrasound in women aged at least 70 when earlier abdominal imaging has not excluded AAA and they have listed risk factors such as smoking, hypertension, family history or arterial disease.
scope_limitations: Conditional opportunistic assessment for women aged 70 or over with a listed risk factor and no previous imaging exclusion; not population-wide screening of women.

reference_title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm: diagnosis and management (NG156)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 19 March 2020 and shows no separate last-updated date.
supported_statement: Offer aortic ultrasound when asymptomatic AAA is being considered in someone outside the NHS screening programme, or when abdominal palpation suggests an aneurysm, to provide disease-specific imaging assessment.
scope_limitations: Supports ultrasound in suspected asymptomatic AAA. Symptomatic or suspected ruptured AAA requires a separate urgent assessment pathway; these statements do not substitute for it.

reference_title: NICE NG148: Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Guideline last update year; recommendation 1.1.1 labelled 2013
supported_statement: In acutely ill adults, diabetes, CKD, hypovolaemia, sepsis and nephrotoxic medicines are among the factors indicating investigation for acute kidney injury.
scope_limitations: AKI investigation criteria replace the seed's generic CKD-progression framing; this source does not substantiate its full hypertension/albuminuria claim or ACOG attribution.

reference_title: NICE NG148: Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Guideline last update year; recommendations labelled 2013
supported_statement: Assess adult AKI using change in serum creatinine from baseline and urine output, with repeat creatinine monitoring; adult diagnostic criteria are not simply eGFR and albuminuria.
scope_limitations: Adult acute-illness context; the eGFR decline criterion in 1.3.1 applies to children and young people. The historical seed is not adopted as source-derived evidence.

reference_title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management (BTS, NICE, SIGN) (NG245)
reference_organization: British Thoracic Society (BTS); National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE); Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 27 November 2024.
supported_statement: In adults with a suggestive asthma history, first measure blood eosinophils or FeNO; either eosinophils above the laboratory range or FeNO at least 50 ppb can confirm asthma.
scope_limitations: Adult pathway; pediatric thresholds differ.

reference_title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management (BTS, NICE, SIGN) (NG245)
reference_organization: British Thoracic Society (BTS); National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE); Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 27 November 2024.
supported_statement: If initial biomarkers do not confirm asthma, use spirometric bronchodilator reversibility in adults; confirmation requires FEV1 improvement of at least 12% and 200 ml, or 10% of predicted normal FEV1.
scope_limitations: Adults with suggestive history after initial biomarker testing.

reference_title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management (BTS, NICE, SIGN) (NG245)
reference_organization: British Thoracic Society (BTS); National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE); Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 27 November 2024.
supported_statement: Confirm asthma only when a compatible history is accompanied by objective test support; document variable respiratory symptoms, triggers, allergic history and possible alternative diagnoses during the initial assessment.
scope_limitations: General initial assessment; objective pathways are age-specific.

reference_title: Asthma: diagnosis, monitoring and chronic asthma management (BTS, NICE, SIGN) (NG245)
reference_organization: British Thoracic Society (BTS); National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE); Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 27 November 2024.
supported_statement: If adult spirometry is unavailable or delayed, record PEF twice daily for two weeks; variability of at least 20% confirms diagnosis. Persistent suspicion despite negative tests warrants consideration of bronchial challenge.
scope_limitations: Adults; PEF variability uses amplitude percentage mean.

reference_title: Atrial fibrillation: diagnosis and management (NG196)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 27 April 2021; updated 30 June 2021. Pulse palpation retains a 2006 label.
supported_statement: If 12-lead ECG misses suspected paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, use 24-hour monitoring for asymptomatic episodes or symptoms less than 24 hours apart; select other ambulatory ECG monitoring or recording technology for less frequent symptomatic episodes.
scope_limitations: AF-specific; does not independently establish flutter assessment. Monitoring applies after an unrevealing 12-lead ECG, not routinely to every arrhythmia.
reference_population: Adults with suspected paroxysmal AF not detected by a 12-lead ECG.
reference_threshold: 24-hour monitor for suspected asymptomatic episodes or symptoms <24 hours apart; other suitable-duration ECG technology for symptoms >24 hours apart

reference_title: Atrial fibrillation: diagnosis and management (NG196)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 27 April 2021; updated 30 June 2021. Pulse palpation retains a 2006 label.
supported_statement: When atrial fibrillation is suspected, assess pulse irregularity by manual palpation; if an irregular pulse is found, use a 12-lead ECG to establish the diagnosis whether or not symptoms are present.
scope_limitations: AF-specific pulse and 12-lead diagnostic pathway; endpoint 51 also includes flutter, not independently substantiated. This is not a general-arrhythmia rule. Post-negative-ECG monitoring is covered separately in ref_0011.
reference_population: Adults with suspected AF, with or without symptoms; an irregular pulse prompts a 12-lead ECG.
reference_threshold: Clinical suspicion prompts pulse palpation; pulse irregularity prompts 12-lead ECG. No numerical diagnostic threshold.

reference_title: NICE NG203: Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication and last update year; recommendation 1.3.4 labelled 2021
supported_statement: CKD monitoring should account for declining eGFR, increasing urine ACR, diabetes and hypertension, alongside the underlying cause and other clinical factors.
scope_limitations: Monitoring and progression assessment in CKD; this does not quantify causal effects or validate the historical ACC/AHA source label.

reference_title: NICE NG203: Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication and last update year; recommendations labelled 2021
supported_statement: Test adults with CKD risk factors using creatinine-based eGFR and urine ACR; ACR is preferred for initial proteinuria detection, with confirmation as specified.
scope_limitations: Applies to CKD assessment, not acute renal failure; risk-group and confirmation requirements must be retained.

reference_title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG115)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 5 December 2018.
supported_statement: For symptomatic people over 35 with suspected COPD, assess smoking history and ask about occupational hazards when considering the diagnosis; smoking is a typical risk factor.
scope_limitations: Smoking and occupational assessment; biomass component unverified.

reference_title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG115)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 5 December 2018.
supported_statement: Confirm suspected COPD using post-bronchodilator spirometry as part of the clinical diagnostic assessment; symptoms and signs determine suspicion and spirometry supports the diagnosis.
scope_limitations: Over-16 diagnosis; not asymptomatic population screening.

reference_title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG115)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 5 December 2018.
supported_statement: Interpret the fixed FEV1/FVC threshold alongside age and symptoms: consider alternative diagnoses in older adults without typical COPD symptoms below 0.7, and consider COPD in symptomatic younger adults above 0.7.
scope_limitations: Ratio alone is insufficient for clinical diagnosis.

reference_title: NICE NG50: Cirrhosis in over 16s: assessment and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Published 6 July 2016; last updated 8 September 2023; recommendation 1.1.1 labelled 2016.
supported_statement: Cirrhosis risk is increased with hepatitis B or C, alcohol misuse, obesity at BMI 30 kg/m2 or higher, and type 2 diabetes.
scope_limitations: Cirrhosis risk in people aged 16 and over, not a claim about every disease of the liver; clinical validity of the historical template remains unreviewed.
reference_population: People aged 16 and over with the specified risk factors for cirrhosis.
reference_threshold: Obesity component defined here as BMI at least 30 kg/m2; other listed factors have no numeric threshold in 1.1.1.

reference_title: NICE NG50: Cirrhosis in over 16s: assessment and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Published 6 July 2016; last updated 8 September 2023; recommendations 1.1.3-1.1.4 labelled 2016, live text uses MASLD.
supported_statement: Cirrhosis investigation uses transient elastography in specified hepatitis C or alcohol-related groups, and elastography or acoustic radiation force imaging for MASLD with advanced fibrosis.
scope_limitations: Cause-specific cirrhosis assessment in people aged 16 and over; not testing for every liver disease. MASLD with advanced fibrosis permits either listed imaging technique.
reference_population: People aged 16 and over with hepatitis C, sustained heavy alcohol consumption, alcohol-related liver disease, or MASLD with advanced fibrosis.
reference_threshold: Alcohol over 50 units/week for men or people registered male at birth, over 35 for women or people registered female at birth, for several months; MASLD advanced fibrosis ELF at least 10.51.

reference_title: NICE NG20: Coeliac disease: recognition, assessment and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication year
supported_statement: Coeliac serology is offered for persistent unexplained gastrointestinal symptoms and to first-degree relatives of affected people, among other specified groups.
scope_limitations: Supports family history and selected symptoms as testing indications; does not verify the seed's broad inflammation claim.

reference_title: NICE NG20: Coeliac disease: recognition, assessment and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication year
supported_statement: Initial serology in young people and adults uses total IgA and IgA tTG; IgA deficiency changes testing. Gluten intake is required during diagnosis.
scope_limitations: Specifies tests absent from the generic seed; this is not a general recommendation for imaging.

reference_title: NICE NG20: Coeliac disease: recognition, assessment and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication year
supported_statement: Young people and adults with positive coeliac serology are referred for specialist intestinal biopsy; persistent suspicion despite negative serology also warrants specialist assessment.
scope_limitations: This records NG20's pathway, not a claim that every contemporary specialist pathway requires biopsy; children have a separate recommendation.

reference_title: Recent-onset chest pain of suspected cardiac origin: assessment and diagnosis (CG95)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 24 March 2010 and last update 30 November 2016; specific recommendation labels distinguish [2010] and [2010, amended 2016] from [2016].
supported_statement: Offer CT coronary angiography with at least 64 slices for typical or atypical angina, or for non-anginal chest pain when an already obtained resting ECG shows ST–T changes or Q waves.
scope_limitations: The stable chest-pain diagnostic pathway specifies these indications. This does not support indiscriminate CT testing for all new cardiac symptoms, acute coronary syndrome, or asymptomatic coronary screening.

reference_title: Recent-onset chest pain of suspected cardiac origin: assessment and diagnosis (CG95)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 24 March 2010 and last update 30 November 2016; specific recommendation labels distinguish [2010] and [2010, amended 2016] from [2016].
supported_statement: For suspected stable angina, document chest-pain characteristics and associated symptoms, then assess whether discomfort is constricting, brought on by exertion, and relieved within about five minutes by rest or glyceryl trinitrate.
scope_limitations: The source evaluates stable chest pain and possible angina. It does not establish coronary atherosclerosis in every patient with cardiac symptoms or describe an asymptomatic screening programme.

reference_title: Recent-onset chest pain of suspected cardiac origin: assessment and diagnosis (CG95)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 24 March 2010 and last update 30 November 2016; specific recommendation labels distinguish [2010] and [2010, amended 2016] from [2016].
supported_statement: When clinical assessment cannot exclude stable angina, obtain a resting 12-lead ECG as soon as possible after presentation; a normal resting ECG alone is insufficient to rule out stable angina.
scope_limitations: ECG assessment for suspected stable angina; no claim that a normal ECG excludes coronary disease. Acute chest pain and possible acute coronary syndrome follow a distinct pathway.

reference_title: Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers (NG97)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 20 June 2018.
supported_statement: Begin suspected dementia assessment with a history of cognitive, behavioural and psychological symptoms and their effect on daily life, obtaining information from the person and, where possible, someone who knows them well.
scope_limitations: Dementia assessment replaces the focal-neurology template mismatch.

reference_title: Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers (NG97)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 20 June 2018.
supported_statement: Refer to a specialist dementia diagnostic service if suspicion persists after investigating reversible causes, including delirium, depression, sensory impairment and cognitive effects of medicines with increased anticholinergic burden.
scope_limitations: Persistent dementia suspicion after investigation of reversible causes.

reference_title: Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers (NG97)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 20 June 2018.
supported_statement: When dementia remains suspected, perform examination, appropriate blood and urine tests for reversible causes, and validated cognitive testing; a normal cognitive instrument score alone does not exclude dementia.
scope_limitations: Non-specialist assessment; normal testing is not exclusionary.

reference_title: NICE NG222: Depression in adults: treatment and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication year; recommendation amended 2022
supported_statement: Depression assessment explores earlier depression, stressful or traumatic events, and drug and alcohol use as influences on development, course and severity.
scope_limitations: Adults undergoing assessment; this is a clinical history recommendation rather than a quantified prospective incidence-risk estimate.

reference_title: NICE NG222: Depression in adults: treatment and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication year; recommendation amended 2022
supported_statement: Assess suspected depression comprehensively, considering severity, history, duration, course and functional impairment instead of relying on symptom count alone.
scope_limitations: Adult depression assessment; a symptom-count-only interpretation of the seed would be inadequate.

reference_title: NICE NG222: Depression in adults: treatment and management
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication year; recommendation 1.2.8 labelled 2009
supported_statement: Ask people with depression directly about suicidal thoughts and intent; considerable immediate risk to self or others requires urgent specialist mental health referral.
scope_limitations: Specifies the risk assessment component; does not certify the historical imputed certainty or strength.

reference_title: Overweight and obesity management (NG246): discussing results and referral
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 14 January 2025 and last update 8 January 2026; recommendation 1.11.1 is labelled [2006, amended 2022].
supported_statement: Explain to adults how the severity of overweight or obesity and central adiposity affects their risk of developing long-term conditions, explicitly including hypertension among the potential future health consequences.
scope_limitations: Supports the seed obesity component only. This recommendation does not independently verify diabetes, chronic kidney disease, or family history as causes of incident hypertension.

reference_title: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management (NG136)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 28 August 2019 and last update 26 February 2026; the year denotes the current guideline version, not the original year of every cited recommendation.
supported_statement: For diagnostic home monitoring, obtain two seated readings at least one minute apart, twice daily for four to seven days; discard the first day and average the remaining readings.
scope_limitations: Specifies how a diagnostic HBPM average is obtained: at least four days, ideally seven. A single home reading is not the diagnostic average.

reference_title: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management (NG136)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 28 August 2019; updated 26 February 2026. Diagnostic recommendations retain their 2019 labels.
supported_statement: Confirm hypertension when clinic blood pressure is at least 140/90 mmHg and the daytime ambulatory average or home monitoring average is at least 135/85 mmHg, using both clinic and out-of-office criteria.
scope_limitations: Diagnostic averages follow prescribed ABPM/HBPM protocols; a single reading is insufficient. No verification of seed grading or primary/secondary aetiology.
reference_population: Adults undergoing systemic hypertension confirmation
reference_threshold: Clinic >=140/90 mmHg AND daytime ABPM average or HBPM average >=135/85 mmHg

reference_title: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management (NG136)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 28 August 2019; updated 26 February 2026. Diagnostic recommendations retain their 2019 labels.
supported_statement: For adults with clinic blood pressure from 140/90 to below 180/120 mmHg, offer ambulatory monitoring to confirm hypertension; use home monitoring when ambulatory monitoring is unsuitable or cannot be tolerated.
scope_limitations: Systemic hypertension diagnosis; severe hypertension follows a separate pathway. No pulmonary, portal or pregnancy-specific evidence.
reference_population: Adults with raised clinic systemic blood pressure
reference_threshold: Raised clinic BP: systolic >=140 OR diastolic >=90 mmHg; this ABPM pathway requires systolic <180 AND diastolic <120 mmHg.

reference_title: Overweight and obesity management (NG246): identifying and assessing overweight, obesity and central adiposity
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 14 January 2025 and last update 8 January 2026; the cited assessment recommendations retain [2022] labels.
supported_statement: NICE classifies overweight at BMI 25–29.9 and obesity from 30 kg/m²; for South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African or African–Caribbean adults, thresholds are 23–27.4 and at least 27.5 respectively.
scope_limitations: The seed BMI 25 kg/m² threshold does not diagnose obesity. Adult classification uses ethnicity-specific thresholds; children need age- and sex-specific assessment.

reference_title: Overweight and obesity management (NG246): identifying and assessing overweight, obesity and central adiposity
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 14 January 2025; last updated 8 January 2026; cited recommendations labelled 2022.
supported_statement: Use BMI to assess adult overweight and obesity, interpreting it cautiously because it does not directly measure central adiposity; add waist-to-height ratio for adults whose BMI is below 35 kg/m².
scope_limitations: Waist-to-height ratio estimates central adiposity and associated risk, not the diagnosis of obesity; adult assessment only.
reference_population: Adults being assessed for overweight, obesity and central adiposity; waist-to-height classification applies at BMI below 35 kg/m2.
reference_threshold: BMI below 35 kg/m2 for combined assessment; waist-to-height ratio 0.5-0.59 indicates increased risk, at least 0.6 further increased risk.

reference_title: Rheumatoid arthritis in adults: management (NG100)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 11 July 2018.
supported_statement: Refer adults with unexplained persistent synovitis for specialist opinion; urgency increases when small hand or foot joints, multiple joints, or a delay of at least three months before seeking care are involved.
scope_limitations: Adult persistent synovitis; not isolated mechanical joint symptoms.

reference_title: Rheumatoid arthritis in adults: management (NG100)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 11 July 2018.
supported_statement: Obtain hand and foot radiographs in adults with suspected rheumatoid arthritis and persistent synovitis; the diagnostic imaging recommendation is linked to persistent synovitis rather than limited to atypical presentations.
scope_limitations: Persistent synovitis; broader than the seed imaging qualifier.

reference_title: Rheumatoid arthritis in adults: management (NG100)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 11 July 2018.
reference_locator: Recommendations 1.1.2 [2009] and 1.1.3 [2009, amended 2018]; investigations introductory text
supported_statement: In suspected rheumatoid arthritis with synovitis on examination, offer rheumatoid factor testing and consider anti-CCP testing when rheumatoid factor is negative; primary-care investigations should not postpone specialist referral.
scope_limitations: Adult suspected RA; tests do not replace clinical assessment.

reference_title: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management (NG128)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NG128 publication year, verified on the official overview; recommendation-specific historical labels are recorded in reference_locator.
supported_statement: Use FAST outside hospital and rapid validated assessment in emergency departments for sudden neurological symptoms, excluding hypoglycaemia; after initial assessment, admit people with suspected stroke directly to a specialist acute stroke unit.
scope_limitations: NG128 acute stroke/TIA scope excludes subarachnoid haemorrhage; FAST screens for possible stroke/TIA and does not establish diagnosis. Other cited assessment and admission recommendations remain conditional on suspected stroke.
reference_population: People aged over 16 with sudden neurological symptoms suggesting stroke/TIA; prehospital and hospital assessment as specified.
reference_threshold: No numeric FAST cutoff; validated symptom recognition and assessment pathways.

reference_title: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management (NG128)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 1 May 2019.
supported_statement: Immediately refer suspected TIA for specialist assessment and investigation within 24 hours of symptom onset; do not use ABCD2 or similar scores to determine referral urgency or subsequent stroke risk.
scope_limitations: Over-16 suspected TIA; time measured from symptom onset.

reference_title: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management (NG128)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication date: 1 May 2019.
supported_statement: Avoid routine CT for suspected TIA unless an alternative diagnosis detectable by CT is suspected; after specialist assessment, consider MRI with diffusion and blood-sensitive sequences, performed that day if selected.
scope_limitations: TIA imaging; acute stroke has a separate pathway.

reference_title: Type 2 diabetes: prevention in people at high risk (PH38)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 12 July 2012 and last update 15 September 2017; the cited recommendations retain [2012] labels.
supported_statement: NICE lists obesity and previous gestational diabetes among conditions associated with increased type 2 diabetes risk, and recommends validated risk questionnaires for adults with risk-increasing conditions, excluding women who are currently pregnant.
scope_limitations: Supports obesity and prior gestational diabetes for the Type 2 diabetes endpoint; family history is not independently verified by this recommendation. Do not extrapolate to type 1 or unspecified diabetes.

reference_title: Type 2 diabetes: prevention in people at high risk (PH38)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 12 July 2012 and last update 15 September 2017; the cited recommendations retain [2012] labels.
supported_statement: Offer venous fasting plasma glucose or HbA1c testing to adults with high risk scores; consider testing South Asian or Chinese adults aged at least 25 whose BMI exceeds 23 kg/m².
scope_limitations: Risk-based type 2 diabetes detection, not universal testing. The specified age, ancestry, and BMI subgroup is an additional consideration, not a diagnostic threshold for diabetes.

reference_title: Type 2 diabetes: prevention in people at high risk (PH38)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NICE page labels publication 12 July 2012 and last update 15 September 2017; the cited recommendations retain [2012] labels.
supported_statement: In asymptomatic people with possible type 2 diabetes, defined here by fasting plasma glucose at least 7.0 mmol/l or HbA1c at least 48 mmol/mol (6.5%), perform a second blood test to confirm.
scope_limitations: The confirmation requirement applies to people without diabetes symptoms. It does not cover every symptomatic presentation, pregnancy, type 1 diabetes, or situations that make HbA1c unreliable.

disease: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung
reference_title: Lung Cancer: Screening
reference_organization: USPSTF
reference_year_basis: Final statement date: 2021-03-09.
reference_locator: Recommendation Summary; Practice Considerations: screening eligibility.
supported_statement: Offer annual LDCT to eligible adults.
scope_limitations: General lung screening; no NSCLC/control inference. Screening context replaces diagnostic seed context.
reference_population: Asymptomatic adults aged 50-80; current smokers or quit within 15 years.
reference_threshold: At least 20 pack-years; annual LDCT.

disease: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung
reference_title: Lung Cancer: Screening
reference_organization: USPSTF
reference_year_basis: Final statement date: 2021-03-09.
reference_locator: Recommendation Summary; Practice Considerations: stopping criteria.
supported_statement: Discontinue LDCT when cessation or health stopping criteria apply.
scope_limitations: General lung screening; no NSCLC/control inference. Screening context replaces diagnostic seed context.
reference_population: Adults enrolled in eligible lung-cancer screening.
reference_threshold: 15 smoke-free years; substantially limited life expectancy or ability/willingness for curative lung surgery.

reference_title: Breast Cancer: Screening
reference_organization: USPSTF
reference_year_basis: Final dated 2024-04-30.
supported_statement: Offer mammography every two years.
scope_limitations: Screening context replaces diagnostic seed context; control exclusions are dataset metadata. Includes family-history/dense-breast risk; excludes high-risk genetic syndromes, prior chest radiation at a young age, previous breast cancer or high-risk lesions.
reference_population: Average-risk persons assigned female at birth; age 40-74.
reference_threshold: Age 40-74; every 2 years.

reference_title: Breast Cancer: Screening
reference_organization: USPSTF
reference_year_basis: Final dated 2024-04-30.
supported_statement: Evidence cannot establish the benefit-harm balance of supplemental ultrasound or MRI.
scope_limitations: I statement; screening scope only. Screening context replaces diagnostic seed context; control exclusions are dataset metadata.
reference_population: Eligible screening population with dense breasts and an otherwise negative mammogram.
reference_threshold: No numeric cutoff; insufficient-evidence statement.

reference_title: Prostate Cancer: Screening
reference_organization: USPSTF
reference_year_basis: Final dated 2018-05-08.
reference_locator: Clinical Summary: Panel 1; linked final: population.
supported_statement: Individualize PSA screening after discussing benefits, harms and preferences.
scope_limitations: Asymptomatic screening replaces diagnostic seed context; control exclusions are dataset metadata.
reference_population: Men without symptoms or previous prostate-cancer diagnosis.
reference_threshold: Age 55-69; no universal PSA threshold specified.

reference_title: Prostate Cancer: Screening
reference_organization: USPSTF
reference_year_basis: Final dated 2018-05-08.
reference_locator: Clinical Summary: Panel 1; linked final: Recommendation Summary.
supported_statement: Recommend against PSA-based screening at age 70 or older.
scope_limitations: Asymptomatic screening replaces diagnostic seed context; control exclusions are dataset metadata.
reference_population: Men without symptoms or previous prostate-cancer diagnosis.
reference_threshold: Age >=70; screening recommendation against.

reference_title: Guideline on haemoglobin cutoffs to define anaemia in individuals and populations
reference_organization: WHO
reference_year_basis: WHO publication date 2024-03-05; PDF title/copyright year 2024.
reference_locator: Normative statements 1.a and 3; Table 2, printed pp. 9/20 (PDF pp. 30/41).
supported_statement: Interpret measured haemoglobin with population-specific cutoffs.
scope_limitations: Supports haemoglobin assessment; does not validate the entire CBC/targeted-laboratory seed. Consider elevation and smoking adjustments; not an aetiological diagnosis.
reference_population: Children 6 months-14 years, including nonpregnant girls; adults 15-65; pregnancy.
reference_threshold: Hb g/L: 6-23mo <105; 24-59mo <110; 5-11y <115; 12-14y boys/nonpregnant girls <120; women15-65 nonpregnant <120; men15-65 <130; pregnancy trimesters1/2/3 <110/<105/<110.

reference_title: WHO guideline on use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status in individuals and populations
reference_organization: WHO
reference_year_basis: WHO publication date 2020-04-21; guideline PDF copyright/title year 2020.
reference_locator: Recommendation 1.2 and Table 1, printed pp. 18-19 (PDF pp. 36-37).
supported_statement: Use age-specific ferritin thresholds when assessing iron deficiency with inflammation.
scope_limitations: Conditional/low-certainty recommendation; interpret inflammation markers. Does not alone establish anaemia; no pregnancy inflammation threshold supplied.
reference_population: Nonpregnant people with infection or inflammation.
reference_threshold: Ferritin µg/L: age<5 <30; age>=5 <70.

reference_title: Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: Screening
reference_organization: USPSTF
reference_year_basis: Final statement date: 2021-08-24.
reference_locator: Recommendation Summary; Practice Considerations: population and screening tests.
supported_statement: Screen eligible adults using HbA1c, fasting glucose or an oral glucose tolerance test.
scope_limitations: Supports HbA1c/FPG screening component; diagnosis and testing thresholds require separate interpretation.
reference_population: Asymptomatic nonpregnant adults in primary care.
reference_threshold: Age35-70; BMI>=25; consider BMI>=23 in Asian Americans and earlier screening in higher-prevalence groups.

reference_title: Tirzepatide for managing overweight and obesity (TA1026)
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Published 23 December 2024; last updated 1 September 2025. Recommendation 1.1 checked in the current published appraisal.
supported_statement: Tirzepatide is an option alongside diet and activity for eligible adults meeting BMI and comorbidity criteria, subject to the commercial arrangement and phased NHS access.
scope_limitations: UK NICE appraisal eligibility and NHS implementation context, not universal prescribing advice or support for the diagnostic template; ethnicity adjustments and phased access matter.
reference_population: Adults eligible for NICE weight management treatment; population and NHS access requirements are separate.
reference_threshold: Initial BMI at least 35 kg/m2 plus at least one weight-related comorbidity; BMI threshold usually reduced by 2.5 kg/m2 for the specified ethnic groups.

reference_title: Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NG97 publication year, verified on the official overview; recommendation-specific historical labels are recorded in reference_locator.
supported_statement: Initial dementia assessment uses symptom history and daily-life impact, with an informant when possible.
scope_limitations: Non-specialist assessment; replaces the focal-neurology template mismatch.
reference_population: People with suspected dementia in non-specialist settings
reference_threshold: None; suspected dementia

reference_title: Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NG97 publication year, verified on the official overview; recommendation-specific historical labels are recorded in reference_locator.
supported_statement: Persistent dementia suspicion warrants examination, appropriate reversible-cause tests and cognitive testing.
scope_limitations: Non-specialist assessment; replaces the focal-neurology template mismatch.
reference_population: Persistent suspected dementia after initial assessment
reference_threshold: Persistent suspicion after initial assessment

reference_title: Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NG97 publication year, verified on the official overview; recommendation-specific historical labels are recorded in reference_locator.
supported_statement: Donepezil, galantamine or rivastigmine monotherapy are options for mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
scope_limitations: Management-only; prescribing conditions 1.5.5-1.5.6 apply.
reference_population: Mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease
reference_threshold: Mild-to-moderate disease

reference_title: Dementia: assessment, management and support for people living with dementia and their carers
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NG97 publication year, verified on the official overview; recommendation-specific historical labels are recorded in reference_locator.
supported_statement: Memantine monotherapy is an option for severe Alzheimer's disease, or moderate disease with AChE intolerance/contraindication.
scope_limitations: Management-only; condition 1.5.5 applies; monotherapy only.
reference_population: Severe Alzheimer's disease; moderate disease with AChE intolerance/contraindication
reference_threshold: Severe disease or AChE-ineligible moderate disease

reference_title: Parkinson's disease in adults
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NG71 publication year, verified on the official overview; recommendation-specific historical labels are recorded in reference_locator.
supported_statement: Motor features can prompt suspicion of Parkinson's disease; refer quickly and untreated for specialist differential diagnosis.
scope_limitations: Age 18 and over; symptoms prompt suspicion rather than establish diagnosis; referral precedes treatment.
reference_population: People aged 18 and over with suspected Parkinson's disease
reference_threshold: Clinical suspicion; quick referral, no fixed numerical interval

reference_title: Parkinson's disease in adults
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NG71 publication year, verified on the official overview; recommendation-specific historical labels are recorded in reference_locator.
supported_statement: Offer levodopa in early Parkinson's disease when motor symptoms affect quality of life.
scope_limitations: Management-only; early diagnosed disease with quality-of-life impact, age 18 and over.
reference_population: Early Parkinson's disease with motor symptoms affecting quality of life; age 18 and over
reference_threshold: Motor symptoms affect quality of life

reference_title: Obstructive sleep apnoea/hypopnoea syndrome and obesity hypoventilation syndrome in over 16s
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NG202 publication year, verified on the official overview; recommendation-specific historical labels are recorded in reference_locator.
supported_statement: Take a sleep history and assess for OSAHS when at least two listed feature groups are present.
scope_limitations: OSAHS only, over 16; not all sleep disorders or central sleep apnoea. Feature groups: snoring; witnessed apnoeas; unrefreshing sleep; waking headaches; unexplained excessive sleepiness/tiredness/fatigue; nocturia; choking during sleep; sleep fragmentation/insomnia; cognitive dysfunction/memory impairment.
reference_population: People over 16 with features suggesting OSAHS
reference_threshold: At least two listed feature groups

reference_title: Obstructive sleep apnoea/hypopnoea syndrome and obesity hypoventilation syndrome in over 16s
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NG202 publication year, verified on the official overview; recommendation-specific historical labels are recorded in reference_locator.
supported_statement: Offer home respiratory polygraphy for suspected OSAHS; use alternative or further testing under the specified access and symptom conditions.
scope_limitations: OSAHS only, over 16. Limited access: consider home oximetry, with accuracy limitations in heart failure/chronic lung disease. Negative oximetry with significant symptoms: consider polygraphy/polysomnography. Impractical home tests or monitoring need: consider hospital polygraphy. Negative polygraphy with continuing symptoms: consider polysomnography.
reference_population: People over 16 with suspected OSAHS
reference_threshold: Access/practicality/monitoring conditions; significant or continuing symptoms after negative tests

reference_title: Recent-onset chest pain of suspected cardiac origin: assessment and diagnosis (CG95)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 24 March 2010; updated 30 November 2016. Individual recommendations have 2010 or 2016 labels.
supported_statement: Use CT coronary angiography of at least 64 slices for typical/atypical angina, or non-anginal pain with resting ECG ST-T changes or Q waves.
scope_limitations: Stable chest-pain pathway only; confirmed CAD with uncertain ischaemic symptoms has a functional-testing pathway. No general acute-coronary or asymptomatic screening rule.
reference_population: Adults assessed for suspected stable angina
reference_threshold: Typical or atypical angina; or non-anginal pain with ST-T changes or Q waves on already obtained resting 12-lead ECG

reference_title: Recent-onset chest pain of suspected cardiac origin: assessment and diagnosis (CG95)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 24 March 2010; updated 30 November 2016. Individual recommendations have 2010 or 2016 labels.
supported_statement: During stable-angina investigation, arrange blood tests for aggravating conditions such as anaemia.
scope_limitations: Ancillary investigation during stable-angina work-up; no universal laboratory panel, haemoglobin cutoff or asymptomatic IHD screening rule.
reference_population: All people being investigated for stable angina
reference_threshold: No numerical threshold specified

reference_title: Chronic heart failure in adults: diagnosis and management (NG106)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 12 September 2018; updated 3 September 2025. Recommendations 1.2.2-1.2.4 retain 2018 labels.
supported_statement: Measure NT-proBNP in adults with suspected chronic heart failure alongside clinical assessment.
scope_limitations: Chronic adult diagnostic pathway; NT-proBNP is not a standalone diagnosis or a universal first test for acute presentations.
reference_population: Adults with suspected chronic heart failure
reference_threshold: No numerical threshold for ordering NT-proBNP in recommendation 1.2.2

reference_title: Chronic heart failure in adults: diagnosis and management (NG106)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 12 September 2018; updated 3 September 2025. Recommendations 1.2.2-1.2.4 retain 2018 labels.
supported_statement: For suspected chronic HF, refer for specialist assessment and transthoracic echocardiography within two weeks at NT-proBNP >2000 ng/L, or six weeks at 400-2000.
scope_limitations: Referral triage for adult suspected chronic HF, not biochemical confirmation, acute-care triage or ejection-fraction classification.
reference_population: Adults with suspected chronic heart failure after NT-proBNP testing
reference_threshold: NT-proBNP >2000 ng/L: within 2 weeks; 400-2000 ng/L inclusive: within 6 weeks

reference_title: Stroke and transient ischaemic attack in over 16s: diagnosis and initial management
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: NG128 publication year, verified on the official overview; recommendation-specific historical labels are recorded in reference_locator.
supported_statement: For suspected TIA, start aspirin 300 mg daily unless contraindicated; refer immediately for specialist evaluation within 24 hours of symptom onset.
scope_limitations: Suspected TIA only, over 16; not all stroke or SAH; management-only, unscored.
reference_population: People over 16 who have had suspected TIA
reference_threshold: Aspirin 300 mg daily immediately; specialist evaluation within 24 hours of symptom onset

reference_title: Pocket Guide to COPD Diagnosis, Management and Prevention: 2025 Report
reference_organization: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD)
reference_year_basis: 2025 edition stated on cover; official linked file is v1.2 final, dated 13 December 2024 in filename.
reference_locator: Printed pages 3 and 5 (PDF pages 6 and 8): Diagnostic Criteria; Diagnosis and Assessment key points
supported_statement: Confirm clinically suspected COPD with post-bronchodilator spirometry showing FEV1/FVC <0.7 in the appropriate symptom/exposure context.
scope_limitations: Clinical diagnosis requires context; isolated ratio or questionnaire scores do not establish COPD. Historical 2025 evidence, superseded by available 2026 edition.
reference_population: Adults with compatible symptoms and/or exposure history suggesting COPD
reference_threshold: Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC <0.7

reference_title: Pocket Guide to COPD Diagnosis, Management and Prevention: 2025 Report
reference_organization: Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD)
reference_year_basis: 2025 edition stated on cover; official linked file is v1.2 final, dated 13 December 2024 in filename.
reference_locator: Printed pages 10-11 (PDF pages 13-14), Figures 2.10 and 2.11; visually checked
supported_statement: After spirometric confirmation of COPD, use CAT to assess symptom and health-status burden beyond breathlessness.
scope_limitations: CAT is supported by the pocket-guide figures; CCQ is not substantiated here. Assessment context extends the diagnostic seed, not an alternative diagnostic test.
reference_population: People with spirometrically confirmed COPD
reference_threshold: No diagnostic questionnaire threshold; ABE figure uses CAT <10 versus >=10 for symptom grouping

reference_title: 2025 Summary Guide for Asthma Management and Prevention
reference_organization: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA)
reference_year_basis: Cover states updated 2025; suggested citation states published June 2025. November URL is hosting path, not a new edition year.
reference_locator: Printed/PDF pages 6-8: Diagnosing Asthma; Figure 1; Table 1
supported_statement: Confirm asthma from variable respiratory symptoms and objective variable expiratory airflow evidence; record the diagnostic basis.
scope_limitations: Adults, adolescents and children 6-11; under-6 diagnosis is outside this summary. Test-specific and age-specific criteria must not be collapsed into one cutoff.
reference_population: Adults, adolescents and children aged 6-11 years with suspected asthma
reference_threshold: No universal numerical threshold; objective test criteria are age-specific (Table 1)

reference_title: 2025 Summary Guide for Asthma Management and Prevention
reference_organization: Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA)
reference_year_basis: Cover states updated 2025; suggested citation states published June 2025. November URL is hosting path, not a new edition year.
reference_locator: Printed/PDF pages 6, 12 Table 2, and 19 Managing risk factors
supported_statement: Assess smoking/vaping exposure as an asthma trigger and exacerbation risk; support cessation and avoidance of other people's smoke/vapes.
scope_limitations: Applies to asthma control and exacerbations in the summary age range, not evidence for incident asthma causation or a quantified exposure-risk threshold.
reference_population: Adults, adolescents and children 6-11 years with asthma
reference_threshold: No numerical tobacco/vaping exposure threshold specified

reference_title: Faecal calprotectin diagnostic tests for inflammatory diseases of the bowel (HTG320; formerly DG11)
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Published 2 October 2013; DG11 migrated to HTG320 in December 2025 with unchanged recommendations; last evidence review 3 May 2017.
supported_statement: Faecal calprotectin is an option in adult IBD/IBS differential assessment when cancer is not suspected and appropriate quality assurance and local care pathways are in place.
scope_limitations: Linked to the suspected IBD component of ulcerative colitis assessment; this does not confirm ulcerative colitis or cover every noninfective colitis. Cancer suspicion falls outside this recommendation.
reference_population: Adults with recent-onset lower gastrointestinal symptoms for whom specialist assessment is being considered, without suspected cancer.
reference_threshold: No universal numeric calprotectin cutoff specified in recommendation 1.1; cancer exclusion, quality assurance and local pathways are eligibility conditions.

reference_title: Osteoarthritis in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG226)
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Published and last reviewed 19 October 2022.
supported_statement: Typical osteoarthritis can be diagnosed clinically without routine imaging at age 45 or older with activity-related joint pain and no stiffness or morning stiffness lasting at most 30 minutes.
scope_limitations: Adult osteoarthritis with typical features; atypical or alternative diagnoses require different assessment. Use exact Arthrosis endpoint 44, not every joint disorder or case variant.
reference_population: People aged at least 45 with activity-related joint pain and the specified morning stiffness pattern.
reference_threshold: Age at least 45 years; absent morning joint-related stiffness or duration no more than 30 minutes.

reference_title: Osteoarthritis in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG226)
reference_organization: NICE
reference_year_basis: Published and last reviewed 19 October 2022.
supported_statement: For osteoarthritis with overweight or obesity, weight loss improves pain, function and quality of life; any loss may help, with 10% likely more beneficial than 5%.
scope_limitations: Management context for established osteoarthritis with overweight or obesity; not a diagnostic cutoff or a claim that obesity causes every arthrosis subtype.
reference_population: People with osteoarthritis who are living with overweight or obesity.
reference_threshold: 10% versus 5% is a comparative weight-loss benefit example, not a minimum eligibility threshold or guaranteed individual outcome.

reference_title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
reference_organization: KDIGO
reference_year_basis: Original April 2024 Kidney International supplement, S117-S314; original 2024 PDF checked directly.
supported_statement: CKD detection assesses both urine albumin and GFR; incidental abnormalities require repeat testing to confirm CKD.
scope_limitations: CKD detection, not all renal failure or AKI; a single abnormal result does not establish chronic disease.
reference_population: People at risk for, or with, CKD; adults and children require their applicable assessment pathways.
reference_threshold: No universal numeric screening threshold in practice point 1.1.1.1; repeat abnormal findings and establish chronicity.

reference_title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
reference_organization: KDIGO
reference_year_basis: Original April 2024 Kidney International supplement, S117-S314; original 2024 PDF checked directly.
reference_locator: Definition/classification and Tables 1-3, printed S137 (PDF page 22); Table 4, S169 (PDF page 54); Practice Point 1.1.3.1
supported_statement: CKD classification considers cause, GFR and albuminuria; diagnosis requires qualifying kidney abnormalities persisting for at least three months, not a single paired measurement.
scope_limitations: CKD classification and decisions; normal or mildly reduced GFR alone does not define CKD. This does not apply CKD chronicity criteria to acute renal failure.
reference_population: People with suspected or established CKD, with chronicity and cause assessed.
reference_threshold: At least 3 months of qualifying abnormalities: GFR below 60 ml/min/1.73 m2 OR kidney damage, including ACR at least 30 mg/g (at least 3 mg/mmol).

reference_title: Pancreatitis (NG104)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 5 September 2018; section 1.2 diagnostic wording clarified June 2025.
reference_locator: Section 1.2 Acute pancreatitis, introductory diagnostic paragraph
supported_statement: Check lipase or amylase in compatible acute pancreatitis; elevations are nonspecific, and CT may confirm inflammation when enzymes are unraised.
scope_limitations: Diagnostic context; provenance unverified.
reference_population: Compatible acute presentation, all ages.
reference_threshold: No numerical enzyme cut-off; CT if unraised.

reference_title: Adrenal insufficiency: identification and management (NG243)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Official NG243 publication date; recommendation 1.2.3 is from the current document.
supported_statement: In people with suggestive unexplained features, recent glucocorticoid withdrawal, selected medicines, autoimmune comorbidities and hypothalamo-pituitary disease increase suspicion of adrenal insufficiency.
scope_limitations: Susceptibility guidance concerns symptomatic initial assessment; it does not establish occurrence risk in an unselected population.
reference_population: People with unexplained features suggesting adrenal insufficiency, including age-specific glucocorticoid exposure groups.
reference_threshold: Recent withdrawal after glucocorticoids for >4 weeks at age >=16 or >3 weeks under 16; other listed factors have no numeric cut-off.

reference_title: Adrenal insufficiency: identification and management (NG243)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Official NG243 publication date; current recommendation 1.2.9 and table 1.
supported_statement: For suspected adrenal insufficiency from age one, obtain morning serum cortisol and interpret assay-specific ranges to guide endocrinology referral or repeat testing.
scope_limitations: Modern immunoassay cut-offs only; oral glucocorticoids at physiological equivalent doses or above preclude testing under this pathway.
reference_population: People aged >=1 year with suspected adrenal insufficiency; not people taking oral physiological-or-higher glucocorticoid doses.
reference_threshold: Sample 08:00-09:00; cortisol <150 nmol/L suggests possible insufficiency, 150-300 uncertain, >300 very unlikely; modern immunoassays only.

disease: Age-related macular degeneration (whether dry or wet)
reference_title: Age-related macular degeneration (NG82)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 23 January 2018; current published recommendations checked.
supported_statement: Suspected AMD becomes more likely with older age, fellow-eye AMD, family history, smoking, hypertension, obesity and specified lifestyle factors.
scope_limitations: Likelihood assessment, not a quantified causal model; includes both dry and wet AMD.
reference_population: People with suspected AMD.
reference_threshold: BMI >=30 kg/m2 is the specified obesity factor; no universal risk score.

disease: Age-related macular degeneration (whether dry or wet)
reference_title: Age-related macular degeneration (NG82)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 23 January 2018; current published recommendations checked.
supported_statement: Use fundus examination for vision changes; suspected active wet AMD needs urgent macular referral and OCT, with conditional fluorescein angiography.
scope_limitations: Early/dry assessment differs from active wet disease; urgent referral applies even without reported visual impairment.
reference_population: People with vision changes or suspected AMD; tests depend on subtype.
reference_threshold: Wet-active suspicion: referral normally within 1 working day; no universal acuity cutoff for diagnosis.

reference_title: Alcohol-use disorders: diagnosis, assessment and management of harmful drinking (high-risk drinking) and alcohol dependence (CG115)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication: 23 February 2011; latest formal update: 21 October 2014; minor link changes April 2026.
supported_statement: Assess suspected alcohol-use disorders using AUDIT and dependence measures such as SADQ or LDQ, together with self/other risks and withdrawal needs.
scope_limitations: Assessment of potential alcohol misuse and dependence; tools are not standalone diagnostic confirmation. Youth require age-appropriate assessment. New reference only; original template provenance and imputed grades remain unverified.
reference_population: People with potential alcohol misuse; guideline covers adults and ages 10 to 17. AUDIT-above-15 comprehensive-assessment recommendation is for adults referred to specialist alcohol services.
reference_threshold: AUDIT score more than 15: consider comprehensive assessment in adult specialist referrals. Adjust dependence/withdrawal criteria for women, older people, children/young people and established liver disease.

reference_title: Generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults: management (CG113)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication: 26 January 2011; selected recommendations dated 2011; last formal update: 15 June 2020.
supported_statement: For suspected generalized anxiety disorder, consider GAD-2 questions and assess distress, functional impairment, and relevant comorbidities comprehensively.
scope_limitations: Adult GAD component only, not all Anxiety disorders. Comprehensive assessment is not based solely on symptom number, severity or duration. New reference only; original template provenance and imputed grades remain unverified.
reference_population: Adults aged 18 and over who may have generalized anxiety disorder, principally in primary care.
reference_threshold: No GAD-2 numeric cutoff stated in recommendation 1.2.2. Consider distress and functional impairment alongside symptoms; no universal risk score threshold is supplied.

reference_title: Pneumonia: diagnosis and management (NG250)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published September 2025; current text includes January 2026 minor amendments; cited assessment recommendations retain specified labels.
supported_statement: For adult community-acquired pneumonia in primary care, assess mortality risk with CRB65 plus clinical judgement.
scope_limitations: CAP severity component; the score does not establish bacterial aetiology. Not for hospital-acquired or ventilator-associated pneumonia.
reference_population: Adults with a clinical CAP diagnosis in primary care.
reference_threshold: CRB65: confusion; RR >=30/min; DBP <=60 or SBP <90 mmHg; age >=65. Hospital referral considered at score >=2.

reference_title: Pneumonia: diagnosis and management (NG250)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published September 2025; current text includes January 2026 minor amendments; cited assessment recommendations retain specified labels.
supported_statement: Avoid routine microbiology in low-severity adult CAP; consider specified cultures and antigen tests in moderate/high severity when indications apply.
scope_limitations: Bacterial investigations within CAP; no assumption that all CAP is bacterial.
reference_population: Adults with CAP; microbiology depends on severity and clinical indications.
reference_threshold: No universal microbial cutoff; low-severity routine testing is not recommended.

reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Barrett’s Esophagus: An Updated ACG Guideline
reference_organization: American College of Gastroenterology (ACG)
reference_year_basis: Original journal issue 1 April 2022; full author manuscript retrieved from PMC. Official ACG directory checked 10 October 2026 lists March 2022 release.
supported_statement: For weekly reflux lasting at least five years with at least three additional Barrett risk factors, consider one screening endoscopy; first-degree family history is included.
scope_limitations: Supports family history; nonspecific inflammation and alarm symptoms are not endorsed as Barrett predictors here.
reference_population: Patients with weekly GERD symptoms ≥5 years and ≥3 additional Barrett risk factors.
reference_threshold: Weekly GERD symptoms ≥5 years plus ≥3: male sex, age >50, White race, smoking, obesity, first-degree BE/EAC history.

reference_title: Diagnosis and Management of Barrett’s Esophagus: An Updated ACG Guideline
reference_organization: American College of Gastroenterology (ACG)
reference_year_basis: Original journal issue 1 April 2022; full author manuscript retrieved from PMC. Official ACG directory checked 10 October 2026 lists March 2022 release.
supported_statement: The ACG diagnostic definition requires at least one centimetre of columnar mucosa and intestinal metaplasia in the tubular oesophagus.
scope_limitations: US definition; UK definitions differ; routine laboratory/imaging assessment unsupported.
reference_population: Patients with endoscopic findings suggesting Barrett oesophagus.
reference_threshold: Columnar mucosa ≥1 cm and tubular-oesophageal intestinal metaplasia; avoid routine normal-Z-line or lesion-free <1 cm biopsies.

reference_title: Bipolar disorder: assessment and management (CG185)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication: 24 September 2014; selected recommendations dated 2014; last update: 2 September 2025.
supported_statement: Assess suspected bipolar disorder with a detailed psychiatric and episode history, comorbidity review, corroborative history, and consideration of alternative diagnoses.
scope_limitations: Adult specialist clinical assessment and differential diagnosis; this does not endorse a standalone disease-specific laboratory test or imputed AAN provenance. New reference only; original template provenance and imputed grades remain unverified.
reference_population: Adults with suspected bipolar disorder assessed in secondary care.
reference_threshold: No numeric diagnostic cutoff in recommendations 1.3.2 and 1.3.3; assessment covers episode history, function, stressors, comorbidities and alternatives.

reference_title: Cataracts (NEI eye-health information)
reference_organization: National Eye Institute, National Institutes of Health
reference_year_basis: Page updated 19 August 2026; official public health information, not a numbered clinical guideline.
reference_locator: Am I at risk for cataracts?
supported_statement: Cataract risk rises with ageing; diabetes, smoking, family history, eye injury and steroid exposure are among listed risk factors.
scope_limitations: Public health information without a guideline recommendation grade; does not cover every cataract subtype.
reference_population: General cataract-risk information; mainly age-related disease.
reference_threshold: No universal numeric exposure or age risk cutoff.

reference_title: Cataracts (NEI eye-health information)
reference_organization: National Eye Institute, National Institutes of Health
reference_year_basis: Page updated 19 August 2026; official public health information, not a numbered clinical guideline.
reference_locator: How will my eye doctor check for cataracts?
supported_statement: An eye clinician can assess cataracts during a dilated eye examination.
scope_limitations: Official patient information supporting the examination component; not a complete clinical diagnostic protocol or surgical eligibility rule.
reference_population: People receiving eye assessment for cataracts.
reference_threshold: No diagnostic numeric cutoff; the separate age-60 screening interval is not a diagnostic threshold.

reference_title: Gallstone disease: diagnosis and management (CG188)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 29 October 2014; current overview records unchanged recommendations following August 2018 surveillance.
supported_statement: Offer liver tests and ultrasound for suspected gallstones; consider MRCP after negative duct-stone ultrasound with duct dilatation or abnormal liver tests.
scope_limitations: Adult gallbladder/bile-duct pathway; not universal endoscopy for cholelithiasis.
reference_population: Adults with suspected gallstone disease or abdominal/gastrointestinal symptoms unresponsive to previous management.
reference_threshold: MRCP: no duct stone on ultrasound plus duct dilatation and/or abnormal liver tests; EUS if MRCP inconclusive. No numeric cut-offs.

reference_title: Pancreatitis (NG104)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 5 September 2018; current guidance includes minor updates through April 2026.
supported_statement: Consider chronic pancreatitis and appropriate referral for chronic or recurrent upper abdominal pain; diagnostic uncertainty may remain after initial investigations.
scope_limitations: Diagnostic referral, not blanket testing.
reference_population: All ages with chronic/recurrent upper abdominal pain.
reference_threshold: Chronic/recurrent upper abdominal pain; no duration/test cut-off.

reference_title: Faecal calprotectin diagnostic tests for inflammatory diseases of the bowel (HTG320)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 2 October 2013; December 2025 migration from DG11 left recommendations unchanged.
supported_statement: Faecal calprotectin is an option for differentiating IBD from IBS in adults with recent lower gastrointestinal symptoms when cancer is not suspected.
scope_limitations: Differential-testing component; neither a Crohn-specific diagnosis nor an indication for routine endoscopy.
reference_population: Adults with recent lower gastrointestinal symptoms for whom specialist assessment is considered.
reference_threshold: Cancer not suspected; quality assurance and locally agreed pathways required. No universal numerical calprotectin cut-off in recommendation 1.1.

reference_title: 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
reference_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes
reference_year_basis: 2026 Standards edition; primary article published online 8 December 2025, doi:10.2337/dc26-S006.
reference_locator: Hyperglycemic Crises: Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention; DKA-specific precipitating-factor and recurrence paragraphs
supported_statement: Missed or inadequate insulin, illness and eating disorders can precipitate DKA; prior DKA and higher HbA1c identify susceptibility in people with diabetes.
scope_limitations: Factor applicability differs by diabetes type and age; this is susceptibility assessment, not a diagnostic rule. Original published ADA text is preserved via PMC.
reference_population: People with diabetes at risk of DKA, particularly insulin-treated people and those with recurrent episodes.
reference_threshold: No numeric cut-off for the selected DKA risk factors in the cited passage.

reference_title: 16. Diabetes Care in the Hospital: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
reference_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes
reference_year_basis: 2026 Standards edition; primary article published online 8 December 2025, doi:10.2337/dc26-S016.
reference_locator: Diabetic Ketoacidosis and Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State; table 16.1 and accompanying diagnostic paragraph
supported_statement: Evaluate suspected DKA clinically and biochemically; diagnosis requires diabetes or hyperglycaemia together with significant ketosis and metabolic acidosis.
scope_limitations: All three domains must be present; existing diabetes permits diagnosis despite glucose below the hyperglycaemia cut-off. Primary article fetched from PMC.
reference_population: People assessed in hospital for suspected DKA, including euglycaemic presentations and either diabetes type.
reference_threshold: Glucose >=200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) OR prior diabetes; beta-hydroxybutyrate >=3.0 mmol/L OR urine ketones >=2+; pH <7.3 AND/OR bicarbonate <18 mmol/L.

reference_title: Diverticular disease: diagnosis and management (NG147)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 27 November 2019; current update page records minor changes through November 2025.
supported_statement: Routine referral for suspected diverticular disease is reserved for unavailable primary-care investigations, suspected colitis, or suspected-cancer criteria.
scope_limitations: Diverticular-disease pathway; does not endorse acute-diverticulitis CT/laboratory rules for the parent condition.
reference_population: Adults aged 18 or over with suspected diverticular disease.
reference_threshold: Refer if routine endoscopic/radiological investigation unavailable from primary care, colitis suspected, or suspected-cancer pathway criteria met.

reference_title: Epilepsies in children, young people and adults (NG217)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication: 27 April 2022; recommendation dated 2022; last update: 5 August 2026.
supported_statement: After a first seizure in adults, assess mental-health problems, vascular risk factors, and sepsis as potentially modifiable indicators of seizure recurrence.
scope_limitations: Second-seizure risk after a first seizure, not epilepsy incidence. Listed factors are adult-specific; association is expressed as potential increased recurrence risk. New reference only; original template provenance and imputed grades remain unverified.
reference_population: Adults presenting with a first seizure; individualized second-seizure assessment also applies to children and young people, but the listed factors are for adults.
reference_threshold: First seizure triggers assessment. No numeric risk cutoff in recommendations 1.1.3 to 1.1.4.

reference_title: Epilepsies in children, young people and adults (NG217)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication: 27 April 2022; selected recommendations dated 2022; last update: 5 August 2026.
supported_statement: After suspected first seizure, assess history, examination, eyewitness information and ECG; consider EEG when epilepsy is suspected, without using EEG to exclude epilepsy.
scope_limitations: First suspected seizure evaluation. ECG assesses cardiac mimics; EEG supports a clinically suspected diagnosis and cannot exclude epilepsy. New reference only; original template provenance and imputed grades remain unverified.
reference_population: Children, young people and adults after a first suspected seizure.
reference_threshold: If requested after a first seizure, EEG should be performed as soon as possible, ideally within 72 hours. No numerical diagnostic cutoff; EEG cannot exclude epilepsy.

reference_title: ACG Clinical Guideline: Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease
reference_organization: American College of Gastroenterology (ACG)
reference_year_basis: Original journal issue 1 January 2022; full author manuscript retrieved from PMC. Official ACG directory checked 10 October 2026 lists November 2021 release.
supported_statement: Use endoscopy first for dysphagia or alarm symptoms; when suspected GORD remains unclear without objective endoscopic evidence, use reflux monitoring off therapy.
scope_limitations: Conditional diagnostic testing; not routine testing of all reflux symptoms or asthma-associated symptoms.
reference_population: Patients with dysphagia/alarm symptoms or uncertain suspected GORD without objective endoscopic evidence.
reference_threshold: Endoscopy for dysphagia, weight loss or gastrointestinal bleeding; off-therapy monitoring for uncertain suspected GORD after no objective endoscopic evidence.

reference_title: Glaucoma: diagnosis and management (NG81)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 1 November 2017; updated 26 January 2022; reviewed 26 March 2025.
supported_statement: COAG assessment combines visual fields, optic-nerve/fundus examination, applanation pressure measurement and anterior-chamber assessment; diagnosis also measures corneal thickness.
scope_limitations: COAG component only; IOP threshold is for referral, not a standalone diagnosis or rule excluding normal-tension glaucoma.
reference_population: Adults assessed for chronic open-angle glaucoma and related conditions.
reference_threshold: Referral: optic-nerve damage OR glaucoma-consistent field defect OR Goldmann IOP >=24 mmHg; consider repeat measures unless urgent.

reference_title: Gout: diagnosis and management (NG219)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 9 June 2022; current published recommendations checked.
supported_statement: Explain gout risk factors including genetics, excess weight, relevant medicines, CKD and hypertension.
scope_limitations: Source-listed factors, without quantified causal effects or validation of template grading.
reference_population: People diagnosed with gout and receiving risk-factor information.
reference_threshold: No universal numeric risk cutoff in this recommendation.

reference_title: Gout: diagnosis and management (NG219)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 9 June 2022; current published recommendations checked.
supported_statement: Assess suspected gout clinically and measure urate; unresolved uncertainty warrants consideration of aspiration/microscopy or specified imaging.
scope_limitations: Urate is interpreted with symptoms and signs; isolated hyperuricaemia does not establish gout.
reference_population: People with symptoms and signs suggesting gout.
reference_threshold: Serum urate >=360 micromol/L (6 mg/dL) supports clinical diagnosis; below this during a flare, repeat >=2 weeks after resolution if suspicion remains.

reference_title: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification (NG238)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Recommendation 1.4.3 explicitly dated [2014], retained in current NG238 published December 2023.
supported_statement: Assess common secondary contributors to dyslipidaemia, including excessive alcohol, uncontrolled diabetes, hypothyroidism, liver disease and nephrotic syndrome, before specialist referral.
scope_limitations: The recommendation concerns investigating secondary causes before referral; it is not a population risk prediction model or a severity estimate.
reference_population: Adults with dyslipidaemia being considered for specialist review.
reference_threshold: No numeric risk threshold in recommendation 1.4.3.

reference_title: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification (NG238)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Recommendation 1.4.2 marked [2014, amended December 2023]; current NG238.
supported_statement: Use clinical findings, a full lipid profile and family history together when evaluating whether an adult has a familial lipid disorder.
