scope_limitations: Supports a defined diagnostic component within broader hyperlipidaemia evaluation; it does not classify every lipid abnormality or infer FH from cholesterol alone.
reference_population: Adults undergoing lipid assessment for possible familial lipid disorder.
reference_threshold: No standalone diagnostic cut-off in this recommendation; assessment must not use strict lipid cut-offs alone.

reference_title: Hyperparathyroidism (primary): diagnosis, assessment and initial management (NG132)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Official NG132 publication date; cited Context passage has no individually dated update.
supported_statement: Women have greater susceptibility to primary hyperparathyroidism than men; this documented sex-related risk component applies specifically to primary disease.
scope_limitations: Contextual epidemiology, not an instruction for universal screening; cannot be extrapolated to secondary or tertiary hyperparathyroidism.
reference_population: Adults aged >=18 who may develop primary hyperparathyroidism, within the guideline scope.
reference_threshold: Context reports women twice as likely as men; no diagnostic or treatment threshold.

reference_title: Hyperparathyroidism (primary): diagnosis, assessment and initial management (NG132)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Official NG132 publication date; current recommendations 1.1.4 to 1.1.6.
supported_statement: For suspected primary hyperparathyroidism, confirm qualifying albumin-adjusted calcium elevations on separate occasions before measuring PTH with a concurrent calcium sample.
scope_limitations: Only the primary-subtype laboratory pathway is supported; this does not authorize secondary/tertiary extrapolation or biochemical diagnosis without clinical context.
reference_population: Adults aged >=18 in primary care with qualifying calcium elevations and suspected primary hyperparathyroidism.
reference_threshold: PTH when adjusted calcium >=2.6 mmol/L on >=2 occasions, OR >=2.5 mmol/L on >=2 occasions with primary disease suspected; measure concurrent adjusted calcium.

reference_title: Thyroid disease: assessment and management (NG145)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Current guideline header last updated 12 October 2023; Context risk passage not individually dated.
reference_locator: Context: Key facts and figures, hypothyroidism paragraph
supported_statement: Hypothyroidism commonly arises from autoimmune Hashimoto thyroiditis, and occurs more often in women and older people in the guideline’s UK population context.
scope_limitations: Background epidemiology and a usual cause are supported; this does not prescribe screening, quantify individual risk, or cover thyroid disease in pregnancy.
reference_population: People with hypothyroidism susceptibility described in the UK population; autoimmune primary disease is the usual cause discussed.
reference_threshold: No risk-assessment cut-off; age-related background prevalence is not a testing threshold.

reference_title: Thyroid disease: assessment and management (NG145)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Current NG145 last-updated header 12 October 2023; recommendations 1.2.8 and 1.2.9 are retained in this version.
reference_locator: Recommendations 1.2.8 and 1.2.9; Terms: Adults and Children and young people
supported_statement: In adults without suspected pituitary disease, begin thyroid testing with TSH and add FT4 when elevated; test both initially for suspected secondary dysfunction.
scope_limitations: Children and young people also require TSH plus FT4 initially; source excludes thyroid disease management during pregnancy and requires context-sensitive interpretation.
reference_population: Adults aged >=16 with suspected thyroid dysfunction; paired TSH/FT4 for suspected pituitary disease or people under 16.
reference_threshold: TSH above laboratory reference range triggers FT4 in the same sample; no fixed numeric diagnostic cut-off in the cited recommendations.

reference_title: The European Insomnia Guideline: An update on the diagnosis and treatment of insomnia 2023
reference_organization: European Sleep Research Society (ESRS) and European Insomnia Network (EIN)
reference_year_basis: Original publisher states first publication 28 November 2023; Journal of Sleep Research 32(6), e14035; DOI 10.1111/jsr.14035.
supported_statement: Assess adult chronic insomnia using clinical and sleep history plus diaries; reserve polysomnography for suspected comorbid sleep disorders or treatment-resistant insomnia.
scope_limitations: Adults over 18 with chronic insomnia. PSG is not necessary or sufficient for insomnia itself; other specified PSG indications also exist. Historical source, not a verified latest-version claim. New reference only; original template provenance and imputed grades remain unverified.
reference_population: Adults over 18 with chronic insomnia, including insomnia with somatic or mental comorbidities; pediatric/adolescent literature was not reviewed.
reference_threshold: Clinical chronic-insomnia minimum: at least three nights weekly for three months, with daytime sequelae despite adequate opportunity. Sleep diary for at least 7-14 days; no upper-duration cap is imposed here. PSG conditional on comorbid-disorder suspicion, resistant insomnia or other specified indications.

reference_title: Irritable bowel syndrome in adults: diagnosis and management (CG61)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 23 February 2008; diagnostic testing recommendations [2008] remain current; red flags amended April 2017.
supported_statement: Use blood inflammatory markers and coeliac testing to exclude alternative diagnoses in adults meeting IBS criteria; routine colonoscopy is unnecessary to confirm IBS.
scope_limitations: Blood tests exclude alternatives; this does not recommend routine endoscopy or treat inflammation as proof of IBS.
reference_population: Adults aged 18 or over meeting the NICE IBS diagnostic criteria.
reference_threshold: Symptoms ≥6 months; pain/discomfort relieved by defaecation or linked to altered bowel frequency/form, plus ≥2: altered passage, bloating/distension, worsening after eating, mucus. No ESR/CRP cut-off.

reference_title: Faecal calprotectin diagnostic tests for inflammatory diseases of the bowel (HTG320)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published 2 October 2013; December 2025 migration from DG11 left recommendations unchanged.
supported_statement: Faecal calprotectin is an option for differentiating IBD from IBS in adults with recent lower gastrointestinal symptoms when cancer is not suspected.
scope_limitations: Differential testing only; not confirmation of IBS or IBD and not an indication for routine endoscopy.
reference_population: Adults with recent lower gastrointestinal symptoms for whom specialist assessment is considered.
reference_threshold: Cancer not suspected; quality assurance and locally agreed pathways required. No universal numerical calprotectin cut-off in recommendation 1.1.

reference_title: Multiple sclerosis in adults: management (NG220)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication: 22 June 2022; recommendation 1.4.2 [2014, amended 2022]; last update: 26 August 2026.
supported_statement: Smoking increases disability progression in people with multiple sclerosis; advise them not to smoke as part of progression-risk management.
scope_limitations: Smoking and disability progression in established MS only; not disease incidence or an unrestricted list of clinical risks and comorbidities. New reference only; original template provenance and imputed grades remain unverified.
reference_population: People aged 18 and over with multiple sclerosis.
reference_threshold: No smoking dose or numerical disability-progression risk threshold specified in recommendation 1.4.2.

reference_title: Multiple sclerosis in adults: management (NG220)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication: 22 June 2022; recommendation 1.1.6 [2022, amended 2026]; last update: 26 August 2026.
reference_locator: Recommendations 1.1.4 to 1.1.6 [2022; 1.1.6 amended 2026]; Update information, June 2026
supported_statement: Evaluate suspected multiple sclerosis using history, examination, MRI and laboratory findings, applying revised 2024 McDonald criteria through specialist neurological assessment.
scope_limitations: Adults with suspected MS. Criteria are referenced, not independently reconstructed; the prior blanket MRI-alone exclusion was removed in June 2026. New reference only; original template provenance and imputed grades remain unverified.
reference_population: People aged 18 and over with suspected multiple sclerosis; diagnosis by a consultant neurologist or specialist under their supervision.
reference_threshold: Follow revised 2024 McDonald criteria. No standalone numeric cutoff is provided by recommendation 1.1.6; assessment combines history, examination, MRI and laboratory findings.

reference_title: Skin Cancer Prevention (PDQ) - Health Professional Version
reference_organization: NCI-hosted PDQ Screening and Prevention Editorial Board
reference_year_basis: Summary updated 8 April 2025; evidence summary, not an NCI/NIH policy statement or numbered practice guideline.
reference_locator: Factors Associated With an Increased Risk of Melanoma: Sun and UV radiation exposure
supported_statement: Intermittent acute sun exposure causing sunburn is associated with increased melanoma risk in observational evidence.
scope_limitations: Melanoma-specific subsection; keratinocyte-cancer and transplant-immunosuppression statements are not extrapolated here.
reference_population: People exposed to intermittent acute sunlight/UV leading to sunburn.
reference_threshold: No quantified exposure cutoff or individual effect estimate.

reference_title: Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (NG12)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published June 2015; updated 15 April 2026; melanoma referral recommendation retains its 2015 label.
supported_statement: Suspicious pigmented lesions meeting the weighted checklist criterion warrant a suspected-melanoma pathway; dermoscopic or nodular suspicion can also warrant referral.
scope_limitations: Referral threshold, not histological confirmation; nodular/nonpigmented lesions have a separate suspicion pathway.
reference_population: People with lesions suggesting cutaneous melanoma.
reference_threshold: Weighted 7-point score >=3; major features 2 each, minor features 1 each; lesion diameter >=7 mm is one minor feature.

reference_title: Melanoma: assessment and management (NG14)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published July 2015; updated July 2022; January 2024 minor BRAF amendments do not alter cited dermoscopy recommendation.
supported_statement: In secondary/tertiary care, trained clinicians use dermoscopy to assess referred pigmented lesions or lesions detected during follow-up.
scope_limitations: Pigmented-lesion assessment component; dermoscopy alone does not claim pathological confirmation.
reference_population: Referred pigmented lesions or lesions identified during melanoma follow-up in specialist care.
reference_threshold: No universal numeric dermoscopy cutoff in recommendation 1.3.1.

reference_title: Headaches in over 12s: diagnosis and management (CG150)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication: 19 September 2012; selected recommendations dated 2012; last formal update: 3 June 2025.
supported_statement: Diagnose migraine from its characteristic headache features and associated symptoms; a headache diary can document frequency, medication use, precipitants, and menstrual timing.
scope_limitations: Clinical migraine diagnosis in people aged 12 and over. Generic disease-specific testing is not established; use age-appropriate headache features. New reference only; original template provenance and imputed grades remain unverified.
reference_population: Young people aged 12 and over and adults presenting with headache.
reference_threshold: Diary at least eight weeks if used. Migraine duration: four to 72 hours in adults; one to 72 hours at ages 12 to 17. Chronic migraine: at least 15 days monthly, at least eight with migraine features, for more than three months.

reference_title: Osteoporosis: risk assessment (NG259)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Official NG259 publication date 29 July 2026; current recommendations and rationale.
reference_locator: Recommendations 1.1.1 and 1.1.4; rationale on systemic glucocorticoids
supported_statement: Ongoing or high-dose systemic glucocorticoids can weaken bones and cause osteoporosis; physiological replacement doses for adrenal insufficiency are excluded from this risk example.
scope_limitations: Source gives glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis rationale; broader fragility-fracture predictors are not asserted to cause osteoporosis.
reference_population: Adults currently or frequently using systemic glucocorticoids, excluding physiological adrenal replacement doses.
reference_threshold: Fracture-risk exposure example: prednisolone >=5 mg daily or equivalent for >3 months, or intermittent higher doses; not an osteoporosis diagnostic threshold.

reference_title: Osteoporosis: risk assessment (NG259)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Official NG259 publication date 29 July 2026; current recommendations 1.4.1 and 1.4.2.
supported_statement: Use DXA bone-density measurement for qualifying previous fragility fractures, and consider DXA to guide decisions when estimated major osteoporotic fracture risk is elevated.
scope_limitations: Conditional osteoporosis-related assessment, not universal screening or diagnosis from fracture history alone.
reference_population: Adults undergoing fragility-fracture assessment; direct previous-fracture DXA pathway applies from age 30.
reference_threshold: Direct DXA: age >=30 with hip/vertebral fragility fracture, one major osteoporotic fragility fracture in last 2 years, or >=2 fragility fractures; consider DXA at 10-year major osteoporotic fracture risk >=10%.

reference_title: Psychosis and schizophrenia in adults: prevention and management (CG178)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Guideline publication: 12 February 2014; selected recommendation [2009, amended 2014]; last update: 4 September 2026.
supported_statement: Evaluate adults with psychotic symptoms through multidisciplinary assessment covering psychiatric history, substance use, medical history, physical examination, trauma, functioning, and self/other risks.
scope_limitations: Secondary-care assessment of psychotic symptoms; differential medical causes must be considered. Psychotic symptoms or first-episode psychosis do not themselves confirm schizophrenia. New reference only; original template provenance and imputed grades remain unverified.
reference_population: Adults with psychotic symptoms undergoing assessment in secondary care.
reference_threshold: No numerical diagnostic cutoff in recommendation 1.3.3.1; use comprehensive multidisciplinary assessment rather than a standalone disease-specific test.

reference_title: Spondyloarthritis in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG65)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published February 2017; updated June 2017; March 2025 medicine amendments do not change cited 2017 diagnostic recommendations.
supported_statement: Family history and recent genitourinary infection are listed SpA risk factors; inflammatory and extra-articular features aid recognition.
scope_limitations: Recognition component; family/inflammatory features prompt suspicion rather than establish diagnosis.
reference_population: People aged 16 and over with possible axial or peripheral SpA.
reference_threshold: No single positive/negative sign or test rules SpA in or out.

reference_title: Spondyloarthritis in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG65)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published February 2017; updated June 2017; March 2025 medicine amendments do not change cited 2017 diagnostic recommendations.
supported_statement: For suspected axial SpA, use sacroiliac radiography unless the skeleton is immature; MRI follows nondiagnostic radiography or immaturity.
scope_limitations: Axial subset only; replaces inappropriate routine endoscopy wording and does not define every peripheral-SpA investigation.
reference_population: People aged 16 and over with suspected axial SpA in specialist assessment.
reference_threshold: Radiographic modified New York criterion: bilateral sacroiliitis grade 2-4 or unilateral 3-4; negative HLA-B27/normal CRP or ESR do not exclude SpA.

reference_title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
reference_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes
reference_year_basis: 2026 Standards edition; primary article published online 8 December 2025, doi:10.2337/dc26-S002.
reference_locator: Screening for Type 1 Diabetes Risk; recommendation 2.7
supported_statement: A family history specifically of type 1 diabetes increases susceptibility and identifies people to offer islet-autoantibody screening for presymptomatic type 1 disease.
scope_limitations: Supports only the family-history component, restricted to type 1 relatives; overweight and previous gestational diabetes in the seed remain unsupported for this claim.
reference_population: People with a family history of type 1 diabetes or known elevated genetic risk; not an undifferentiated metabolic-risk population.
reference_threshold: No quantitative family-history threshold in recommendation 2.7; no BMI or gestational-diabetes criterion for this component.

reference_title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
reference_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes
reference_year_basis: 2026 Standards edition; primary article published online 8 December 2025, doi:10.2337/dc26-S002.
supported_statement: Use HbA1c or plasma glucose to confirm diabetes; use standardized islet autoantibodies to clarify type 1 classification in adults with overlapping phenotypes.
scope_limitations: Biochemical thresholds diagnose diabetes, not its type; presymptomatic type 1 screening requires autoantibodies rather than HbA1c alone.
reference_population: Nonpregnant people being diagnosed with diabetes; islet-antibody classification recommendation applies to adults with overlapping diabetes phenotypes.
reference_threshold: HbA1c >=6.5% (48 mmol/mol) OR fasting plasma glucose >=7.0 mmol/L after >=8-hour fast; two abnormal results required unless unequivocal hyperglycaemia; no subtype-specific glucose cut-off.

reference_title: Venous thromboembolic diseases: diagnosis, management and thrombophilia testing (NG158)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Published March 2020; updated August 2023; reviewed May 2026 without replacing the cited diagnostic recommendations.
supported_statement: Suspected leg DVT is assessed with the two-level Wells score, followed by score-appropriate ultrasound and D-dimer pathways.
scope_limitations: DVT component of VTE; PE has a separate pathway. Wells estimates probability and does not establish diagnosis.
reference_population: Nonpregnant adults with symptoms/signs of suspected leg DVT.
reference_threshold: DVT likely: Wells >=2; unlikely: <=1. Likely pathway ultrasound result within 4 hours if possible; delayed imaging uses the specified interim pathway.

reference_title: Vitamin B12 deficiency in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG239)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Official NG239 publication date 6 March 2024.
reference_locator: Box 2: common risk factors for vitamin B12 deficiency
supported_statement: Low vitamin B12 intake, selected autoimmune or gastrointestinal conditions, and certain medicines can increase susceptibility to vitamin B12 deficiency.
scope_limitations: Supports nutritional deficiency and specifically named conditions only; does not validate blood loss, all chronic disease, or inevitable anaemia.
reference_population: People aged >=16 at risk of vitamin B12 deficiency, including those with anaemic presentations.
reference_threshold: No numeric threshold for listed risk factors in box 2.

reference_title: Vitamin B12 deficiency in over 16s: diagnosis and management (NG239)
reference_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
reference_year_basis: Official NG239 publication date 6 March 2024.
supported_statement: Investigate suspected B12 deficiency with total or active B12 testing, applying specific initial-test exceptions and concentration ranges rather than relying on a blood count.
scope_limitations: Pregnancy requires active B12; suspected nitrous-oxide cause requires homocysteine or MMA initially. Anaemia is not required for deficiency.
reference_population: People aged >=16 with suspected B12 deficiency; distinct pregnancy and recreational nitrous-oxide pathways.
reference_threshold: Total B12 <180 ng/L (133 pmol/L) or active B12 <25 pmol/L indicates deficiency; total 180-350 ng/L or active 25-70 pmol/L is indeterminate; validated local total-B12 thresholds may apply.
